changes.text: 格兰特回信说，他没有谈和的权限，南方放下武器就能让和平早日到来。此后李再次来信，可这封信送得很费劲：由于格兰特所走的路线，这封信很可能无法在约定时间内送到他手里并带回答复，除非信使穿过南军战线。米德和谢里登都对是否停火非常犹豫，怕这不是真心求和；而且北弗吉尼亚军团已无路可逃，除非用诡计脱身。因为路线的缘故，李派人护送带信的军官穿过自己的战线，把信送到格兰特手里。

Grant replied that he had no authority to treat on the subject of peace, and that by laying down their arms the South would hasten peace. Lee then wrote again, but this message was hard to deliver: from the route Grant had taken, it would probably not be possible to reach him and get an answer back within the time fixed unless the messenger passed through the rebel lines. Meade and Sheridan both hesitated very considerably about suspending hostilities at all. They were afraid the overture was not in good faith; and the Army of Northern Virginia was where it could not escape except by some deception. Because of Grant's route, Lee sent an escort with the officer bearing the message through his own lines to Grant.

dispositions.rationale: 原文的主语只是「they」，没有指明是谁无法及时联系上格兰特。因此删去中文的“对方”和英文的“Lee's side”，改成不指定主体的说法：这封信很可能无法按时送达并带回答复。同时按原文补回限定条件“除非信使穿过南军战线”。中英两版同步修改，段内其他句子不变。

evidence.quote: from the route I had taken, they would probably not be able to communicate with me and get an answer back within the time fixed unless the messenger should pass through the rebel lines
